Assisting patients with any type of cancer, across any age group.

Rise Above - Capital Region Cancer Relief makes life a little easier by providing financial assistance and support to cancer patients in the Canberra and Queanbeyan Palerang Region. We are uniquely able to provide assistance to patients diagnosed with any type of cancer, across all ages. 

Rise Above has been assisting patients in the Canberra/Queanbeyan region for 40 years and our team knows how incredibly difficult it is to juggle the added costs associated with cancer treatment on top of everyday living.

We provide financial assistance to for medication relating to current treatment for cancer, dietary supplements, food & petrol vouchers, electricity accounts, fertility preservation and UC Cancer Wellness Clinic.

WHO ARE WE
Rise Above - Capital Region Cancer Relief, is a not-for-profit organisation established to provide financial assistance and support to cancer patients and families residing with them within the ACT, Queanbeyan and surrounds.
Helping patients feel safe and supported when cancer is diagnosed, by providing unbiased financial support.

The Cancer Support Group (Rise Above) began in 1985 when Yvonne Cuschieri started raising funds to enable 13 local teenagers to attend a CanTeen national camp. It wasn’t long before social workers asked Yvonne to help other families who were facing crisis situations due to cancer.

In March 1986, Yvonne invited friends to help, and the first Cancer Support Group meeting was held in her dining room.

Over the years, the number of requests for help constantly increased. Yvonne and volunteers ran all operations of The Cancer Support Group for 15 years until the workload required additional full-time staff to organise fundraisers and administration.

We adopted the name Rise Above – Capital Region Cancer Relief in 2017 to focus on supporting our amazing patients from the Capital region to rise above and fight cancer.

We rely on the local community

As a charitable organisation, we rely on fundraising, community partners, the generosity of businesses and the local community, to meet the needs of the increasing number of families that require our assistance.

DONATE NOW
By lessening the financial burden of cancer, the patient can concentrate on treatment and their mental wellbeing.

Today, Rise Above assists hundreds of patients yearly and are continually looking for opportunities to facilitate better outcomes for local cancer patients and their loved ones; understanding that by lessening the financial burden of cancer, the patient can concentrate on treatment and their mental wellbeing.

TAKE A LOOK
Karen's story
...the mathematical certainty of unalleviated poverty...

One cannot work. If you are unfortunate enough to have a brain tumour early, which many people do, the opportunity to build life's buffer of savings, super and assets... the things we do for the Rainy Days...simply doesn't occur. There is no insurance cover. There are no part time jobs. There isn't a juicy and generous superannuation payout and life-long benefits.

The generous charity of Rise Above provides us with an extra $200 each month. We are 5 months in. The support package is designed to last about 12 months. The difference this small amount makes is simply incalculable.

OUR STAFF & BOARD MEMBERS
Rise Above Staff
Renee Watson

Chief Executive Officer

Renee brings energy, compassion, and extensive experience leading organisations that exist to improve lives. Born and raised in Queanbeyan, Renée spent much of her career in the UK, first at Oxford University helping to build the National Cancer Research Network, and then as a social entrepreneur, inspiring children to have fun with hands-on science. 

Renee is happiest working with communities, bringing diverse people and perspectives together to turn complex challenges into meaningful, human-centred solutions. Having trained as a scientist here in Canberra, and shaped by decades in the not-for-profit and social impact space, she helps organisations grow sustainably while staying closely connected to the people they serve. 

Renee is excited to return to the community where it all began, driven by her belief in dignity, equity and the power of community to effect positive change.

Belinda (Bin) Barnier

Senior Community Relationship Manager 

As a passionate health advocate and former cancer patient, I understand firsthand the challenges of a cancer diagnosis and treatment.

With over 30 years raising funds, building teams and engaging with the community in the not-for-profit sector, it’s an honour to join the Rise Above team and build on the legacy established over the past 38 years in Canberra and the region.

Whilst undergoing treatment for triple negative breast cancer (TNBC) during COVID, I was able to witness both the strengths and weaknesses of our local community services and the impact a cancer diagnosis can have on individuals and their families.

During chemotherapy in 2020, I was too ill to work, and our family was stretched to the limit. The support provided by Rise Above made life easier, allowing me to focus on treatment and recovery. Rise Above provided funds to assist us to purchase groceries, fuel and medications. My appreciation for this assistance will remain with me for life and I am committed to ensuring other cancer patients receive the same consideration, so life can be a little easier.

With the demand for assistance increasing each year, it’s more important than ever, that we come together as a community to minimise the emotional and financial burden of a cancer diagnosis.

I look forward to creating ways of supporting those in need and ensuring that no one faces the challenge alone.

Stephanie Kulpa

Patient Support Coordinator

Stephanie is a compassionate and dedicated professional whose personal experience with cancer has deeply influenced both her life and career.

She holds a Bachelor of Social Work from Loyola University Chicago and brings nearly five years of experience as a Mental Health Worker in Queanbeyan. Since joining Rise Above in 2022, Stephanie has remained committed to supporting others in meaningful ways, driven by her genuine passion for helping people.

Karina Bruce

Patient Support Coordinator

Karina brings over 30 years of financial administration experience, raising 3 wonderful children, jointly helped build the current family home and has created and operated several businesses.

Whilst completing the house in 2018, she was diagnosed with breast cancer, this has provided her with a firsthand understanding of the challenges faced by those impacted by illness, whilst shaping her approach to leadership and community service. 

Karina’s dedication and commitment ensures that every initiative undertaken is grounded in integrity and a genuine desire to make a positive difference. Blending professional expertise, real life experience and heartfelt dedication, she inspires those around her and helps foster a culture of hope and resilience within Rise Above to support others, where her actions are also guided by compassion and empathy.

Karen Gruber

Patient Support Officer

Karen has spent much of her career working in Human Resources within the public service, alongside also dedicating many years to volunteer work in the local community.

A long-time volunteer with Lifeline, Karen spent years supporting callers on the phones, developing a deep appreciation for the importance of compassion, connection and simply being there to listen when people need it most.

Karen brings a wealth of care, empathy and community spirit to Rise Above and is passionate about supporting local people through the challenges of cancer treatment. She looks forward to connecting with patients and helping ensure they feel heard, supported and never alone.

Rise Above Board Members

Our Board is made up of a group of diverse and inspiring individuals committed to Rise Above. All Directors volunteer their time to bring a wide range of business, lived, and commercial experience. The Board Members oversee the strategic direction of Rise Above, along with compliance and governance.

Tharanie Vithanage

Chair of the Board

Tharanie is committed to ensuring that patients and families get accurate diagnosis, information and care and the peace of mind to be able to manage and survive cancer.

She is a lawyer by trade, and has previously been in the Australian Army, the Australian Customs and Border Protection Service and the Australian Border Force. She is currently a public servant at a Commonwealth Department and an Army Reserve officer. Her roles have given her experience in issues relating to governance, corporate/workforce, operational, planning, ministerial and media.

Tharanie is a qualified lawyer and a senior public servant in the Commonwealth. She has lived all over the world and posted around with the military but now has called the Eden-Monaro area home for about 14 years.

Leesa Ffrench

President

Leesa’s journey with Rise Above began when her brother-in-law was diagnosed with cancer. Witnessing the invaluable support provided by Rise Above, she was inspired to get involved and make a difference.

As the Accounts Manager for Express Truck Service in Queanbeyan, Leesa has leveraged her position to foster a strong partnership between her company and Rise Above. Express Truck Service has proudly sponsored numerous fundraisers organised by Rise Above and other community groups working on their behalf.

Since joining the Rise Above team, Leesa has been a key contributor, dedicating her time and expertise to various aspects of the organisation. From fundraising and volunteering to providing accounting assistance and supporting the staff, her efforts have significantly bolstered the charity’s mission.

Leesa is deeply committed to Rise Above and looks forward to continuing her efforts to raise funds and support those in need. 

Leesa believes in the power of collective action, stating, "Together, we can kick cancer!"

Len Hatch

Vice President

As a result of cancer treatment last year, Len became aware of and mightily impressed by the support and services provided by Rise Above. 

With experience over recent years on various Boards, he reached out to Rise Above to offer his services. Prior to retirement, Len pursued a diverse range of roles, including 15 years as a Union Official in the South Australian car industry, advising three Cabinet Ministers over a 25 year period, conducting his private consultancy in Industrial Relations, Human Resources and Communications, and finally a decade in the Australian Public Service in various corporate roles (Human Resources, Communications and, Governance) at Geoscience Australia, Department of Immigration (Learning and Development) and the National Health and Medical Research Council (Strategic Communications). 

Upon retirement, Len joined the Ainslie Football Club Board in 2015 after serving in various manager, coach and other volunteer roles with junior teams. His three children all participated at junior level with the Club. In retirement Len has been heavily involved in other volunteer roles, with St Vincent de Paul, Belconnen Community Services and since late 2021, as a Board member with Warehouse Circus. 

In 2022 he was elected to the role of President. In 2023, I Len was asked to join the St Vincent de Paul Social Justice Committee. Len has a strong commitment to community, and working with NFP organisations, and is proud to have joined the Board of Rise Above.

Kristina Crnagoj

Director

Kristina is a proud resident of Canberra (Ngunnawal / Ngambri Country) who has lived in the Territory for over 25 years. 

She currently holds a governance position in a Commonwealth Public Service and prior to this worked in a number of operational roles in the Australian Border Force and the Department of Home Affairs. 

Kristina started her professional career as a mental health nurse and during that time was employed in a range of nursing roles across Australia and the United Kingdom.

Kristina was nominated to the Rise Above Board in November 2023. She has a great love of working with people and is looking forward to using the skills she has developed throughout her professional career to support the significant and amazing work of Rise Above.

Stuart Coates

Secretary

Stuart is a seasoned leader with extensive experience in project management, governance, and community engagement. As a Senior Manager at a Consulting firm, he drives strategic initiatives that strengthen delivery maturity, risk management, and organisational development. His professional expertise includes building auditable governance frameworks, refining risk registers, and embedding scalable processes that enhance accountability and transparency across complex projects.

Beyond his corporate career, Stuart has dedicated nearly a decade to volunteering across the not-for-profit sector. He has supported children and families impacted by cancer through Camp Quality and Canteen, contributed to mental health awareness initiatives with Running for Resilience, and assisted with major fundraising events for Lifeline Canberra. His approach to leadership is grounded in clarity, collaboration, and continuous improvement, with a strong focus on empowering teams and fostering inclusive volunteer environments.

Stuart brings to the Board a unique blend of professional governance expertise and lived experience in the volunteer sector, ensuring that community organisations are equipped with the structures and support they need to thrive.

David Wilden

Director

David currently serves on several Advisory Committees supporting refugees and migrants as well as serving on Boards for NGO organisations such as Interplast in addition to Rise Above. He is also currently a Global Fellow with the Migration Policy Institute and a Fellow with the Centre for Policy Development, while also an active member of the Ministers Expert Panel on Skilled Migration. 

David served for over 20 years in a range of senior executive positions in the Australian Public Service. From 2014 to his ‘semi’ retirement in late 2022 he led divisions covering Immigration and Citizenship Policy, International Policy and most recently the Refugee, Humanitarian and Settlement Division.

He was a key contributor for Australia in the consultations and negotiations for the Global Compact for Migration and has been the Australian representative on a number international fora. He previously served as Regional Director for Europe for the Department of Immigration and Citizenship, based in London.

David has always been active within the community, mainly through supporting as a coach, committee member or chair, various sporting groups that his children were involved in. 

Having lost his mother to cancer, he is committed to the goals of Rise Above.

Samara Gentle

Board Member

Samara has lived and worked in the Canberra and Queanbeyan region for over 20 years. Samara brings over a decade of experience in the not-for-profit sector, with a strong focus on strategic fundraising and donor engagement. She has held leadership roles at both state and national levels with the St Vincent de Paul Society, driving innovation in donor acquisition and sustainable revenue growth.

Samara serves in a senior fundraising strategy role at a specialist fundraising agency, where she advises national and international charities on how to grow their supporter bases and maximise long-term impact. Her portfolio includes work with leading organisations such as Canteen, The Salvation Army and Vision Australia.

With a passion for data-driven strategy and a values-led approach, Samara is committed to helping organisations build sustainable income streams so they can continue to grow their impact well into the future.

Diana Fernandes 

Board Member

Diana Fernandes brings a wealth of governance, regulatory, and advocacy expertise to Rise Above. With a distinguished background in compliance and resilience across FTSE 100 institutions and public sector organisations, Diana champions values-driven leadership and systemic change in every role she undertakes.

Her experience spans strategic governance, stakeholder engagement, and operational excellence - with a keen focus on aligning ethical decision-making with meaningful community impact. Diana’s appointment reflects her unwavering commitment to supporting vulnerable communities and advancing trauma-informed care principles through inclusive governance models.

As a Board Member, she is honoured to serve the Canberra region and contribute to Rise Above’s mission of providing practical, emotional and financial relief to those rising above cancer.

Mainul Haque OAM

Board Member

Mainul is an economist and governance professional with nearly 30 years of experience across government, academia, and the not-for-profit sector. Throughout his career, he has held senior roles within the Australian Public Service, including the Department of the Prime Minister and Cabinet and the Treasury, where he led significant national policy initiatives spanning tourism, climate change, employment, and education.

A dedicated social justice advocate, Mainul has extensive experience in governance, strategic policy development, and community engagement. He has served as the ACT Multicultural Ambassador, a board member of ACTCOSS, ACT Multicultural Advisory Committee and President of the Canberra Muslim Community, where he led the development and delivery of the multi-million dollar Gungahlin Mosque – a major community initiative uniting over 40 different ethnicities.

Mainul currently serves on several boards and committees, including the Order of Australia Association (ACT Branch), Gungahlin College, ACT Place Names Advisory Committee, and Community Radio 2XX. In 2023, he was awarded the Medal of the Order of Australia (OAM) for his services to the multicultural community in Canberra.

Having seen the profound impact that practical and compassionate support can have on individuals and families, Mainul is honoured to join Rise Above to help empower those affected by cancer to navigate their journeys with dignity and hope.

Shara Reid

Board Member

Shara is a senior legal, governance, risk and compliance professional with extensive experience in providing strategic leadership and advice to organisations. Specialising in risk management, governance frameworks and compliance processes. 

Qld admitted legal practitioner, independent member - audit and risk management committee member Qld Department of Justice and Attorney General

Rise Above Ambassadors

Our Ambassadors are a passionate and diverse group of community members who generously volunteer their time and expertise to support Rise Above’s mission. With a powerful mix of lived experience, professional insight and practical skills, they help shape our vision and ensure our work is guided by integrity, accountability and compassion. Their dedication helps strengthen our community and ensures that no one faces cancer alone. Together, we continue to build a network of hope, support, and resilience.

Mijica Lus

Ambassador

Mijica Lus is a dedicated community advocate, legal professional, and youth leader. She currently works in the ACT Legislative Assembly and is completing her Juris Doctor at the University of Canberra. With a background in outreach, youth work, and community services, Mijica brings lived experience and a strong voice to the issues that matter from domestic violence support to cultural empowerment and climate justice.

Originally from Papua New Guinea and raised across the Pacific, Mijica now calls the ACT home. She has led grassroots initiatives supporting Pasifika and regional communities, including film festivals, book drives, and cultural workshops through the Aurosokwo Project—an organisation she funds and manages independently.

Mijica is also the ACT Representative for Pacific Climate Warriors and serves on several national and regional advisory groups, including those focused on multicultural health, volunteering, and youth leadership.

With a strong sense of justice shaped by her upbringing and community work, Mijica is passionate about creating more inclusive systems and opportunities for marginalised communities.

“I believe in the power of lived experience to guide meaningful change. It’s an honour to contribute to spaces that uplift community voices, especially those often left out of the conversation.” - Mijica Lus.

RISE ABOVE JOBS

Do you share our determination to make life better for people with cancer? See our available positions below.

Community Vibes Co-ordinator

Could you get excited about doing something that feels good, does good and raises hope in our community? We are looking for our first Community Vibes Coordinator to amplify Rise Above’s mission by making our events extraordinary, coordinating our team of volunteer Risers, raising awareness of cancer through real local people’s stories and helping us to raise vital funds.

OUR LIFE MEMBERS

Rise Above recognises the contribution of longstanding members with ‘Life Membership’. These dedicated people have put their time, energy, expertise, and enthusiasm into Rise Above to help us to provide better outcomes for local cancer patients.

We thank each Life Member for their dedication to our mission, purpose, and values.

Yvonne Cuschieri OAM

The late Yvonne Cuschieri founded The Cancer Support Group (Rise Above) in 1986. Yvonne and volunteers ran all operations for 15 years until the charity grew to the extent where two additional full-time staff were required.

Joe Cuschieri

Joe assisted Yvonne with the running of The Cancer Support Group (Rise Above) for 15 years. Joey was a vital volunteer for the charity, he committed himself to every fundraising event and organised extra assistance from voluntary workers when required.

Robyn Murphy OAM

The late Robyn Murphy helped Yvonne organise and run fundraising events for the group since the early stages of the charity’s development. Robyn assisted in the growth of the group throughout her life.

Paul Walshe OAM

Paul was on the Board of Directors since its initiation in 2006. Paul’s Hawaiian Ball raised over $200,000 for the Group over the years and he contributed a significant amount of time and resources into Rise Above.

Paul is now the Chair of the Board for Respite Care for Queanbeyan, Yvonne's Dream.

Hugh Percy

Mr Hugh Percy has showcased outstanding and enduring service to the charity as a Board member since 2004, and Chair from 2006 to 2018. Hugh stepped down from the Board at the 2019 AGM

FINANCIAL ASSISTANCE

Something iconic is coming to Queanbeyan… and it’s going to change the game. Literally.

Are you a business or community group located in Queanbeyan, Googong, Carwoola or Jerrabomberra? 
Get involved and be part of this once‑in‑a‑generation project!
Secure your Street!

From Mayfair to Old Kent Road, you can bid in our online auction to secure your street on the Queanbeyan Monopoly Board. 

Streets, Community Chest and Chance cards, as well as the money in the Bank, are all up for grabs
Bidding opens at 8 am on the 13th April 2026
Bidding closes at 5 pm on the 4th May 2026
Desperate for a particular possie on the board? You can choose buy it now as soon as the auction opens

Please see full Terms and Conditions here

CHECK OUT THE AUCTION
Eligibility

All bidders and purchasers must:

Hold a valid ABN or be an incorporated entity.
Be a Queanbeyan, Carwoola, Jerrabomberra, or Googong–based and/or owned business or organisation, or be actively trading within the local region.
Ensure the person bidding has full authority (or delegated authority) to commit the business/organisation to the purchase.
Accept the online auction process, noting that all bids are final.
Read and accept all Terms & Conditions (below) prior to bidding or purchasing.

The Agreement will only be amended to reflect the Purchaser’s details and the purchase price.

Check out the full FAQs below

Why participate?

Queanbeyan Monopoly is a true celebration of our region and community. Participating organisations will get:

Your logo, photo and name printed on the board on your chosen street
a 100 word overview of your organisation, logo and QR code in a full-colour booklet with every game
announcements of successful street purchases on Rise Above social media and local news coverage
Bespoke game with photos of beautiful local landmarks, unique artwork specially designed for the project by local artist 
Custom playing pieces, including one piece designed by local primary school students
3000 board games ready for Christmas 2026!
CHECK OUT THE AUCTION
FAQs
Where do proceeds go?

All proceeds go to Rise Above Capital Cancer Region Relief. Founded 40 years ago in Queanbeyan, Rise Above provides financial, emotional, and practical support to local cancer patients. All funds go straight to helping families in our region.

Why be on the board?

Being part of the Monopoly Queanbeyan Edition is a unique opportunity to secure a permanent place in a game that will be played, shared, and remembered for generations.

With only a limited number of boards produced, your business or organisation becomes part of Queanbeyan history — featured alongside iconic local places in a globally recognised game. Your name and logo appear directly on the board, with additional exposure through a business profile and QR code included in every game booklet.

Beyond visibility, being on the board is a meaningful way to demonstrate your commitment to the local community. Every space purchased directly supports families in our region who are facing cancer, turning your involvement into real, lasting impact.

This is more than advertising. It’s community pride, local legacy, and tangible support — all rolled into one powerful project.

Your impact by street colour

By purchasing a street, you can make a real and lasting impact:

Light Blue Street = 1 patient and their family supported for up to 12 months
Yellow Street = 3 patients and their families supported for up to 12 months
Blue Street = 5 patients and their families supported for up to 12 months

How to purchase 

 You can purchase the game through this website with pre-orders available in the second half of this year. In person purchases will be available at the Rise Above office located at 21 Cooma Street, Queanbeyan and at some participating retailers (TBC). Keep an eye out on this website and through the Rise Above socials for more information.

In regards to the purchase of a space or card on the board, this will be available via an online auction link. Please refer to the ‘Auction process’ for further information.

Auction process

To ensure a fair and transparent process for everyone, all Monopoly Queanbeyan Edition spaces will be sold via an online auction. This approach allows all eligible participants to access the same information, view current bids in real time, and bid with confidence knowing the process is open and equitable.

The auction operates in a format similar to eBay. Registered bidders can view available spaces, place bids, and receive updates on the status of their bids throughout the auction period. Each space has a reserve price, which is set to reflect its value and impact. As with standard auction practice, reserve prices are not visible to bidders.

In addition to bidding, some spaces may include a ‘Buy Now’ option at a clearly stated, fixed price. If a bidder chooses to use the Buy Now option and completes payment, the space is immediately secured and no further bids will be accepted for that item.

Each auction will be open for a set period, with opening and closing times clearly displayed on the auction site. Access to the auction is via a unique link, ensuring participation is limited to eligible businesses and organisations only.

This process has been designed to balance fairness, transparency, and opportunity — while ensuring the strongest possible outcome for the local families this project supports.

Who is eligible to purchase a space/card in the Monopoly Queanbeyan Edition?

Eligibility is limited to businesses, clubs, organisations and entities that are owned and/or based in Queanbeyan, Carwoola, Jerrabomberra or Googong, and that comply with the Conditions of Participation and Purchase set out in the Terms & Conditions.

Can I buy more than one space? 

No. Each individual, business or organisation is limited to the purchase of one (1) space per ABN or incorporated entity as part of the Monopoly Queanbeyan Edition initiative.

Do the spaces have the same value and conditions as the equivalent traditional Monopoly spaces?

Yes. All spaces are identical to traditional Monopoly spaces in terms of value and gameplay. The only variation is the inclusion of the purchaser’s business or organisation name and logo on the board space and corresponding card.

Is there a Reserve price?

Yes. We have set a reserve price for each space being offered for auction.

What is the minimum bid increment?

The minimum bid increment is $100 per space. This is clearly displayed for each space on the auction site at the time of bidding.

Will there be a ‘Buy Now’ option?

Yes. All board spaces include a Buy Now option at a clearly set price. Community Chest and Chance cards are available via Buy Now only and are not offered for bidding.

If I use ‘Buy Now’, can someone else take the space? 

No. When you select Buy Now and complete your purchase, the space is secured for you and is no longer available to other bidders.

If I ‘BUY NOW’ do I have to pay in full? 

Yes. This requires payment in full on receipt of an invoice from Rise Above.

What are the payment terms if I am successful in purchasing? 

If you are successful in securing a space (either through bidding or Buy Now), payment is required in accordance with the Terms & Conditions. Full details, including timeframes and accepted payment methods, are outlined in the T&Cs.

What happens if I change my mind and no longer want the space I have purchased? 

If you choose not to proceed after purchasing a space, the purchase will be forfeited and any payment made will not be refunded, in line with the Terms & Conditions. Rise Above reserves the right to resell the space.

What happens if Rise Above don’t sell all the spaces? 

If all spaces are not sold, Rise Above may reopen the remaining spaces for a final auction period. If the required number of spaces is still not secured, the game may not proceed and any funds received will be returned to purchasers, in accordance with the Terms & Conditions.

What goes on my board space? 

Your business/entity name and logo and/or photo will be on the space and corresponding title deed/mortgage card. See the photos below as an example.

Who is the agent for Hasbro?

The Monopoly Queanbeyan Edition is produced through Winning Moves Australia https://winningmoves.com.au/custom-games/

Ready to roll?
BID NOW!
Raising vital funds for Rise Above

In our 40th year, Rise Above is possibly more needed now than ever in its history. 

We are now serving over 800 local cancer patients each year, that's 1/3 of ALL cancer patients in the region. 

This project will help to ensure that we can continue making life a little easier for people undergoing possibly the toughest time of their lives.

If you have questions please call on 6297 1261 or email monopolyqbn@outlook.com

As an immigrant in Australia, I only have my husband as family here. As much as we've always been financially organized, we could never have prepared ourselves for the months to come... They played an important role in relieving some of the stress that we didn’t even know we could face during this time."

PRIVACY POLICY
POLICY STATEMENT 

The ACT Eden Monaro Cancer Support Group (ABN 68 997 342 984), trading as “Rise Above – Capital Region Cancer Relief” (Rise Above) is committed to transparency, accountability and good governance, and endeavours to handle personal information in accordance with this Privacy Policy (the Policy) and the Australian Privacy Principles. 

PURPOSE 

This Policy describes how Rise Above handles personal information it collects.

POLICY 

Rise Above is categorised as a small business operator, and, given the nature of the personal information it collects, it seeks to handle such information in a manner consistent with this Policy and the Australian Privacy Principles. 

Rise Above considers the privacy of personal information it holds in respect of the patients to whom the charity provides charitable services, particularly health information, to be of the greatest importance. 

Rise Above may revise this Policy from time to time by updating the relevant section of its website. The revised Policy will take effect when it is posted on the website. 

AUTHORISATION

Kim Stonham acting Chair of the Board 

21 March 2023 

RESPONSIBILITIES

The CEO is the Privacy Officer for Rise Above. 

It is the responsibility of CEO to ensure that: 

employees, members and volunteers are aware of this policy, and 
any breaches of this policy coming to the attention of the CEO are dealt with appropriately. 

It is the responsibility of all employees, members and volunteers to ensure that their usage of personal information held by Rise Above conforms to this policy, and that any breaches coming to their attention are brought to the attention of the CEO at the earliest possible moment. 

DEFINITIONS

“personal information” has the same meaning given to that term in clause 6 of the Privacy Act 1999 (Cth), 

"sensitive information” has the same meaning given to that term in clause 6 of the Privacy Act 1999 (Cth), 

“small business operator” has the same meaning given to that term in clause 6D of the Privacy Act 1999 (Cth), 

PROCESSES

What is “personal information”? 

In this Policy, “personal information” includes information or an opinion about an identified person, or a person who is reasonably identifiable: 

whether the information or opinion is true or not, and 
whether the information or opinion is recorded in a material form or not. 

Personal information includes ‘sensitive information’, which Rise Above may handle from time to time, including in the circumstances described by this Policy. 

What kinds of personal information does Rise Above handle? 

The types of personal information Rise Above will collect and maintain will depend on how you interact with us, but will generally include name, date of birth, gender, contact information (including address, telephone numbers and email address), credit/debit card information, health information, other information about a person’s history with, or relationship to cancer and other information about the nature of a person’s interactions with Rise Above. 

Rise Above may collect other personal information from time to time, in accordance with this Policy and the Australian Privacy Principles. 

Whose personal information is collected? 

Rise Above collects personal information from people who are connected to its operations and activities – including employees, contractors, donors, members, volunteers, sponsors, recipients of charitable services, health professionals, suppliers, service providers, governments and participants in advocacy campaigns or health promotion projects. 

How is personal information collected?

Most often, Rise Above collects personal information directly from the person concerned. This may be in person, in written form, on the telephone, or online. 

Rise Above may also obtain personal information from third parties such as contractors (including fundraising service providers), vendors, health professionals, social and community workers. If Rise Above collects personal information about a person from a third party and it is unclear that the person has consented to the disclosure of their personal information to Rise Above, reasonable steps will be taken to contact the person and ensure that they are aware of the circumstances surrounding the collection and purposes for which their personal information has been collected. 

Why is personal information collected?

Rise Above may collect, hold, use and disclose personal information for a number of purposes, including: 

support services: to provide charitable services and information, and to evaluate and report on these, 
administrative services: maintaining membership and volunteer records, 
marketing and promotion: to communicate about donations, events, products, services, campaigns, and causes, 
volunteering and other support: to enable people to assist Rise Above with volunteering, community fundraising, advocacy and other activities where we seek the community’s assistance, 
health promotion: to provide information about cancer risk factors (such as sun, tobacco and obesity), and to seek support for campaigns, and 
other issues: communicating in relation to Rise Above operations, activities and objectives, to verify a person’s identity, to improve and evaluate Rise Above programs and services and to comply with relevant laws. 

Where Rise Above collects personal information for a specific purpose not outlined above, it will provide the person concerned with a collection notice which explains the primary purpose and any related secondary purposes for which it is collecting their personal information. 

Health information and other sensitive information

As part of administering charitable services, Rise Above may collect: 

health information (for example, current and historical medical information of a person seeking charitable services from Rise Above) and, 
other sensitive information (for example marital/relationship status which may indicate sexual orientation). 

Rise Above will limit the collection of sensitive information to the minimum amount required to provide its charitable services. 

What happens if personal information is not provided?

If a person does not provide some or all of the personal information requested, Rise Above may not be able to offer them services or provide them with information about Rise Above activities, causes, events, programs and projects. 

Website usage information and cookies

When a person accesses the Rise Above website (https://riseabovecbr.org.au/), software may be in use, embedded in the website (such as Javascript). Rise Above may place small data files (or cookies) on the user’s computer or other device to collect information about which pages they view and how they reach Rise Above, what they do when they visit a page, the length of time they remain on the page, and how Rise Above performs in providing content to them. 

A cookie does not identify individuals personally, but it does identify computers. The user can set their browser to notify them when they receive a cookie and this will provide them with an opportunity to either accept or reject it in each instance. Rise Above may gather the user’s IP address as part of its business activities and to assist with any operational difficulties or support issues with its services. This information does not identify the user personally. 

Rise Above may use a web analytics service to monitor web traffic such as Google Analytics. A web analytics service informs how visitors use the Rise Above website based on their browsing habits, so that improvements can be made to the website to make it easier for visitors to find the information they are seeking. External providers of web analytics services, such as Google, may also receive this information as a visitor browses the website. If a visitor would like to optout of being tracked, they can do so be using Ad Settings or by using the Google Analytics Optout Browser Addon (so they are not tracked by Google Analytics). 

This Policy applies to Rise Above’s website only, and does not apply to any third party websites that may be linked from Rise Above’s website or social media pages. If a person navigates to a third party’s website from Rise Above’s website, that person will be subject to the third party’s privacy policy, and will not be covered by this Policy. 

Opting out of direct marketing communications

Where Rise Above uses personal information to send marketing and promotional information by post, email or telephone, it will provide recipients with an opportunity to opt-out of receiving such information. By electing not to opt-out, Rise Above assumes it has their implied consent to receive similar information and communications in the future. Rise Above will always ensure that opt-out notices are clear, conspicuous and easy to take up. 

If a person does not wish to receive direct marketing communications from Rise Above, they should contact Rise Above, PO Box 1351, Queanbeyan NSW 2620, Tel: 02 6297 1261 or email: admin@riseabovecbr.org.au. 

To whom does Rise Above disclose personal information?

Rise Above may disclose personal information to its employees, members and volunteers and members of the Board in their Board capacity. 

Health information and other sensitive information is handled with a higher degree of confidentiality, and is disclosed to employees, members or volunteers on a ‘need to know’ basis (at the discretion of the Chief Executive Officer of Rise Above). That is, the information is disclosed to assist the recipient of the information to undertake activities which will directly or indirectly enable the provision of charitable services by Rise Above to the person who is the subject of the information. Rise Above will not disclose health information and other sensitive information to a third party (other than a member, volunteer or third party providing data hosting facilities and/or services) without the prior consent of the person concerned. 

Rise Above may need to disclose personal information to others in order to carry out its activities. This may include: 

Contractors and service providers who perform services on behalf of Rise Above, such as mailing houses, printers, information technology services providers (including offshore cloud computing service providers), database contractors and telemarketing agencies. 
Third parties for marketing purposes: Rise Above may provide a person’s contact details to other like-minded organisations to contact the person with information that may be of interest to them. 
External support services: to health care professionals, lawyers, accountants, other professionals, counsellors, funders, financiers, co-ordinators, members, volunteers, service providers, agencies and not-for-profits that provide support services. 
The governments of New South Wales and the Australian Capital Territory, also the Queanbeyan-Palerang Regional Council, and any other local government authority which Rise Above has dealings with. 
Where Rise Above is compelled to disclose the information by law, or where Rise Above has reason to suspect that unlawful activity, or serious misconduct that relates to Rise Above’s functions or services has been, is being or may be engaged in. 
Where a person(s) has provided his/her/their consent to the disclosure. 

Wherever Rise Above proposes to disclose personal information to a third party not outlined above, it will provide the person concerned with a collection notice which explains the circumstances in which it might disclose their personal information. 

Cross-border disclosures of personal information

Rise Above may use data hosting facilities and third party service providers to assist it with providing goods and services. As a result, personal information may be transferred to, and stored at, a destination outside Australia, including but not limited to New Zealand, Netherlands, China, Singapore, Hong Kong, Ireland, Canada, United States of America and the United Kingdom. 

Personal information may also be processed by staff or by other third parties operating outside Australia who work for Rise Above or for one of its suppliers, agents, or partners. Rise Above takes such steps as are necessary in the circumstances to ensure that any overseas third party service providers deals with personal information in a manner consistent with the Australian Privacy Principles, including through contractual arrangements. 

If a person’s personal information is collected using a collection notice that references this Policy, they are taken to consent to the disclosure, transfer, storing or processing of their personal information outside of Australia. They also acknowledge and understand that by providing such consent that Rise Above will not be required to take such steps as are reasonable in the circumstances to ensure such third parties comply with the Australian Privacy Principles. 

Where is personal information stored?

Rise Above takes all reasonable steps to protect all of the personal information it holds from misuse, interference and loss, and from unauthorised access, modification or disclosure. Personal information will be stored on a password protected electronic database, which may be on a database maintained by Rise Above, a database maintained by a cloud hosting service provider or other third party database storage or server provider. Backups of electronic information are written to drives which are stored offsite. 

Hard copy information is generally stored in offices of Rise Above, which are secured to prevent entry by unauthorised people. Any personal information not actively being used is archived, usually for 7 years, and may be held with a third-party provider of secure archiving services. 

Where personal information is stored with a third party, Rise Above has arrangements which require those third parties to maintain the security of the information. Rise Above takes reasonable steps to protect the privacy and security of that information, but is not liable for any unauthorised access or use of that information. Personal information will stay on the database indefinitely until advice is received that a person would like it removed, unless it is de-identified or destroyed earlier in accordance with privacy law requirements. 

Direct debit or credit cards 

Rise Above uses Stripe as an online portal for all financial transactions involving donations and registrations. The Rise Above website does not take financial details from anyone. Please contact Stripe (privacy policy (stripe.com)) for its privacy policy when submitting an online transaction for donations and registrations with Rise Above. 

Access to personal information 

Rise Above will, upon request, and subject to applicable privacy laws, provide a person with access to their personal information that is held by it. However, Rise Above requests that the requester identify, as clearly as possible, the type(s) of information requested. Rise Above will deal with the request to provide access to personal information within 30 days and the requester agrees Rise Above may charge them reasonable costs incurred in supplying them with access to this information. 

Rights to access personal information are not absolute and privacy laws dictate that Rise Above are not required to grant access in certain circumstances such as where: 

access would pose a serious threat to the life, safety or health of any individual or to public health or public safety, 
access would have an unreasonable impact on the privacy of other individuals, 
the request is frivolous or vexatious, 
denying access is required or authorised by a law or a court or tribunal order, 
access would be unlawful, or 
access may prejudice commercial negotiations, legal proceedings, enforcement activities or appropriate action being taken in respect of a suspected unlawful activity or serious misconduct. 

If Rise Above refuses to grant a person access to their personal information, it will provide them with reasons for that decision (unless it is unreasonable to do so) and the avenues available for them to complain about the refusal. 

Updating personal information 

A person may ask Rise Above to update or correct the personal information held about them at any time. Rise Above will take reasonable steps to verify the person’s identity before granting access or making any corrections to their information. Rise Above also has obligations to take reasonable steps to correct personal information it holds when it is satisfied that it is inaccurate, out- of-date, incomplete, irrelevant or misleading for the purpose for which it is held. 

If a person requires access to, or wish to update their personal information, please contact Rise Above, PO Box 1351, Queanbeyan NSW 2620, Tel: + 61 2 6297 1261 or email: admin@riseabovecbr.org.au. 

Complaints

If a person has any queries or would like to make a complaint regarding relating to this Policy or the manner in which personal information has been handled, please contact Rise Above’s Privacy Officer, on 02 6297 1261 or email ceo@riseabovecbr.org.au. The Privacy Officer endeavours to respond to complaints and queries within fourteen calendar days of their receipt. If a person is dissatisfied with the response of Rise Above, they may refer the matter to the Australian Information Commissioner (see www.oaic.gov.au). 

Data breaches

The Chief Executive Officer is responsible for the management of data breaches. All significant data breaches are reported to the Board of Rise Above. 

Rise Above will notify individuals when there is a data breach (that is, when there is unauthorised access or disclosure) that involves their personal information, and that a reasonable person would conclude that the breach would be likely to result in serious harm to the individuals to who the information relates. Rise Above will not notify individuals that a data breach has occurred where as a result of remedial action taken by Rise Above in relation to the breach (before it results in serious harm to any individual to whom the information relates) a reasonable person would conclude that the unauthorised access or disclosure of the information would not be likely to result in serious harm to any of those individuals. 

Data breaches can be caused or exacerbated by a variety of factors, affect different types of personal information and give rise to a range of actual or potential harms to individuals, agencies and organisations. As such, Rise Above does not have a single way of responding to a data breach. Each breach will be dealt with on a case-by-case basis, undertaking an assessment of the risks involved, and using that risk assessment as the basis for deciding what actions to take in the circumstances. 

Data breaches will be managed in accordance with the following framework: 

Contain the breach, undertake a preliminary assessment and determine who needs to be notified immediately, 
Evaluate the risks associated with the breach, considering: a. the type of personal information involved, 
the context of the affected information and the breach, 
establish the cause and extent of the breach, 
assess the risk of harm to the affected individuals, 
assess the risk of other harms, 
Notification, considering the who, what, when, why and how in terms of notifying affected individuals, and 
Prevent future breaches, taking the time to investigate the cause and consider whether to review the existing data breach prevention plan or, if there is no plan in place in a specific instance, developing one.

Change Order Details

Please place your order carefully as we are unable to change or update a delivery address or products once an order has been processed, so please be sure to check your delivery and product details prior to submitting your order. When the delivery address has been supplied incorrectly or the incorrect product is chosen, the cost of having the item(s) re-delivered will be charged to the customer. Please email us at admin@riseabovecbr.org.au for further instructions.

Product & Specifications

Features and specification of products described or depicted on the website, are subject to change without notice. All images are for illustration purposes only and may vary from the product received. Size of each product on this website are not shown in their actual size.

Prices & GST

All our prices are in Australian Dollars (AUD). Prices are subject to change without notice. GST is included in all eligible products, however once an item which attracts GST is purchased, GST will apply to the whole of the postage and handling.

Payment

All payments must be finalised prior to delivery of goods. Rise Above does not accept cheque, cash or vouchers for online payments. If you wish to use one of these payment methods, please visit us at 21 Cooma Street QUEANBEYAN NSW 2620.

Providing Feedback

When providing feedback, please let us know the following information: Your Name and Email Address, Brief description of the issue and date of purchase (if applicable), Order Number, Product name and serial number (if applicable).

Contact Us

If you have any questions or feedback, please call our office on (02) 6297 1261 or email us at admin@riseabovecbr.org.au - Our team aims to respond to your inquiry within 24 business hours.

Refund policy

We have a 12-day return policy, which means you have 12 days after receiving your item to request a return or exchange.

To be eligible for a return, your item must be in the same condition that you received it, unworn or unused, with tags, and in its original packaging. You’ll also need the receipt or proof of purchase.

To start a return, you can contact us at admin@riseabovecbr.org.au - We’ll send you instructions on how and where to send your package.Items sent back to us without first requesting a return will not be accepted.

Damages and issues

Please inspect your order upon receiving and contact us immediately if the item is defective, damaged or if you receive the wrong item, so that we can evaluate the issue and make it right.

Refunds

We do not offer refunds unless the item is faulty.However, a credit note will be issued for returns if your size is not available.We will notify you once we’ve received and inspected your return, and let you know if the refund or credit note was approved or not.If approved, you’ll be automatically refunded on your original payment method, or a credit note will be sent via email.Please remember it can take some time for your bank or credit card company to process and post the refund too.
